ru-5-1.text: Is there an information-exchange process between shifts regarding quality, current production issues, and key topics (when more than one shift exists)? Are health and safety requirements considered when planning work?
ru-5-1.examples: Expected evidence: Shop-floor quality meetings and minutes; shift handover method.

ru-5-2.text: Are daily meetings held on production issues (quality, output, breakdowns, etc.)?

ru-5-3.text: Are all workstations supplied with accessible visual work instructions?
ru-5-3.examples: Expected evidence: Work instructions, checklists, set-up sheets

ru-5-4.text: Are work instructions readily available and legible where used?

ru-5-5.text: Is 5S implemented? Are cleaning schedules maintained for workshops, workstations, and equipment?
ru-5-5.examples: Expected evidence: Cleaning schedule, housekeeping standard.

ru-5-6.text: Do workstations meet health, safety, and ergonomics requirements?
ru-5-6.examples: Expected evidence: Environmental/workplace assessment (lighting, noise, etc.); workstation certification where applicable.

ru-5-7.text: At workstations, is documented evidence available for monitoring product and processes per the control plan?
ru-5-7.examples: Expected evidence: Inspection/test methods and result records (forms/IT).

ru-6-1.text: Are inspection methods defined for incoming materials and purchased parts against key characteristics?
ru-6-1.examples: Expected evidence: Inspection methods and result records.

ru-6-2.text: Are supplier test reports complete, available, and current?
ru-6-2.examples: Expected evidence: Receiving inspection: type, periodic, and acceptance test results.
docs: Receiving inspection records (type tests, periodic tests, acceptance tests)

ru-6-3.text: Are golden samples / masters agreed for incoming parts and materials (where applicable)?

ru-6-4.text: Setup verification / first-piece approval: control of first good part after startup, downtime, changeover, batch change, etc. Are verification records retained?
ru-6-4.examples: Expected evidence: Setup log/settings records and first-article verification records.

ru-6-5.text: Are responsibilities for first-article verification defined and are personnel trained?
ru-6-5.examples: Expected evidence: Training acknowledgement for personnel performing first-article checks.
docs: Training acknowledgement for personnel performing first-article checks

ru-6-6.text: Are documented acceptance criteria established for first-article approval with unambiguous criteria?
ru-6-6.examples: Expected evidence: Control plan/method specifying first-article acceptance criteria.
docs: Control plan/method specifying first-article acceptance criteria

ru-6-7.text: Is there a documented reaction plan for process/product deviations? Are environmental and occupational health aspects considered where relevant?
ru-6-7.examples: Expected evidence: Reaction plan addressing key equipment failure; disruption of outsourced products/processes/services; natural disasters; fire; utility interruptions; cybersecurity incidents affecting IT; labour shortage or infrastructure disruption.
docs: Reaction/contingency plan covering key scenarios (equipment failure, disruptions, cybersecurity, utilities, staffing, infrastructure)

ru-6-8.text: Are nonconforming product data in production collected and analyzed?
ru-6-8.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure and sample statistical analysis records.

ru-6-9.text: Are corrective actions taken to eliminate causes of nonconforming product (with effectiveness verified and horizontally deployed to similar processes)?
ru-6-9.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample corrective action records.

ru-6-10.text: Are inspection methods and acceptance criteria documented for all manufacturing stages?
ru-6-10.examples: Expected evidence: Inspection methods and result records.

ru-6-11.text: Is statistical process control (SPC) applied to key characteristics where required?
ru-6-11.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure and sample charts/records.

ru-6-12.text: Are records retained for verification of product/process characteristics through the production cycle (receiving, in-process, final inspection)?
ru-6-12.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample verification records.

ru-6-13.text: Are control record retention periods defined per customer requirements and internal guidelines?
ru-6-13.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure defining retention periods.
docs: Standard or procedure defining retention periods

ru-6-14.text: Are rules documented for identification and segregation of nonconforming product?
ru-6-14.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample records.

ru-6-15.text: Are disposition rules documented and applied for nonconforming product: rework, scrap, concession, disposal, etc.?
ru-6-15.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample disposition records.

ru-6-16.text: Is nonconforming product storage (quarantine/Hold area) identified and access-controlled?
ru-6-16.examples: Expected evidence: Quarantine/Hold area and status labelling.

ru-7-1.text: Are calibration/recalibration intervals defined in documented information per manufacturer recommendations, customer requirements, and instrument wear?
ru-7-1.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure and sample calibration records.

ru-7-2.text: Are measuring instruments calibrated; is calibration status clearly indicated in writing?

ru-7-3.text: Is there a procedure and records for measurement system analysis (gage R&R/stability studies) demonstrating measurement system suitability?
ru-7-3.examples: Expected evidence: MSA procedure and studies for gauges/tooling.

ru-7-4.text: Are measurement systems fit for intended use with objective evidence per MSA results?

ru-7-5.text: Is each measuring instrument identified with a unique ID and next calibration due date?

ru-7-6.text: Are visual defect standards (samples/photos of nonconformance) available to inspection personnel?
ru-7-6.examples: Expected evidence: Defect catalog / boundary samples.

ru-8-1.text: Does top management hold quality-focused meetings evidenced by minutes, and intervene when milestones are delayed or targets are not met?
ru-8-1.examples: Expected evidence: Meeting landscape; minutes with resulting corrective/improvement actions.

ru-8-2.text: Are rules defined for reacting to external product complaints?
ru-8-2.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample complaint handling records.

ru-8-3.text: Are past significant issues logged in a knowledge database? Is ownership defined? Is the database updated when defects are detected?

ru-8-4.text: Are all complaints addressed using the 8D methodology?
ru-8-4.examples: Expected evidence: Tracking register and sample 8D report.

ru-9-1.text: Are all key characteristics error-proofed (poke-yoke) where feasible?
ru-9-1.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with example device records.

ru-9-2.text: Is periodic verification of mistake-proofing device effectiveness performed?

ru-10-1.text: Is a contingency plan established for disruptions (utilities, epidemics, key equipment breakdown, etc.) to protect shipment stability?
ru-10-1.examples: Expected evidence: Reaction plan addressing key scenarios (equipment, outsourced disruptions, disasters, utilities, staffing, infrastructure).

ru-10-2.text: Have personnel been made aware of actions to take during atypical disruptions affecting delivery stability?
ru-10-2.examples: Expected evidence: Training/awareness on contingency plan with evidence of understanding.

ru-11-1.text: Does finished goods packaging comply with customer requirements?
ru-11-1.examples: Expected evidence: Document specifying requirements (customer packaging label/DCL/spec).

ru-11-2.text: Does packaging adequately protect finished goods?
ru-11-2.examples: Expected evidence: Document specifying requirements (customer packaging label/DCL/spec).

ru-11-3.text: Is there a barcode/labelling process for product ready for shipment to the customer?
ru-11-3.examples: Expected evidence: Document specifying barcode/labelling requirements.

ru-11-4.text: Do handling and storage methods prevent mixing of different materials or components?
ru-11-4.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with example records.

ru-11-5.text: Do handling and storage methods prevent omission of manufacturing operations?

ru-11-6.text: Can purchased materials and components be traced to batches used in finished product?
ru-11-6.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample traceability records.

ru-11-7.text: Are warehouse items clearly labelled and legible?
ru-11-7.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample labels/tags.

ru-11-8.text: Are WIP/semi-finished items identified either on the parts or containers?

ru-11-9.text: Is FIFO enforced at warehousing, manufacturing, and shipping stages?
ru-11-9.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with example FIFO verification.

ru-11-10.text: If FIFO relies on IT, can FIFO be sustained manually/paper/visual when IT fails?

ru-11-11.text: Are storage conditions (temperature, humidity, shelf life) met and logged? Are environmental instruments calibrated and due dates tracked?
ru-11-11.examples: Expected evidence: Parameter logbook; calibration of monitoring devices.

ru-12-1.text: Are supplier selection and evaluation criteria defined (initial and periodic)?
ru-12-1.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample evaluation records.

ru-12-2.text: Is there a reaction plan for poor periodic supplier ratings and a supplier development plan to improve supplier quality/process capability?
ru-12-2.examples: Expected evidence: Supplier rating output; development/action plan.

ru-12-3.text: Is supplier PPAP/production approval aligned with PPAP or customer-specific requirements?
ru-12-3.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure with sample PPAP approvals.

ru-12-4.text: Do suppliers resolve complaints using the 8D methodology?
ru-12-4.examples: Expected evidence: Supply agreement / SQ requirements.

ru-12-5.text: Is receiving inspection aligned with the control plan, or alternatively after a supplier quality deviation notification? Are results recorded and validated by responsible management?
ru-12-5.examples: Expected evidence: Control plan and receiving inspection records.

ru-12-6.text: How is immediate feedback provided when nonconforming product is detected at inbound/receiving?
ru-12-6.examples: Expected evidence: Supply agreement / escalation rules.

ru-12-7.text: Are delivery quality requirements defined in contract (e.g. quality agreement)?
ru-12-7.examples: Expected evidence: Supply agreement / quality appendix.

ru-13-1.text: Are documented procedures in place for control of documented information (creation, approval, change, obsolete withdrawal)?
ru-13-1.examples: Expected evidence: Standard, procedure, or documented process.

ru-13-2.text: Is there a documented information master list/register showing revision status?
ru-13-2.examples: Expected evidence: QMS document matrix with monitoring/updating.
docs: QMS documented information matrix/list with revision status monitoring
